name: Santander
summary_text: No department-specific legal, enforcement or incident finding was located for this division. The 2025 national reporting groups it with departments where anti-LGBTIQ+ violence has expanded territorially while the state response stayed insufficient — one LGBTIQ+ person was killed every 32 hours nationally in 2025 (270 killings, a 63% increase on 2024's 164, of which 18% of the 2024 homicides were trans women). Otherwise it inherits national conditions.

sources.title: The transphobic murder that has shocked Colombia | International | EL PAÍS English
sources.claim_summary: English-language report (14 Apr 2025) on the murder of trans woman Sara Millerey, 32, in Bello, Antioquia (4 Apr 2025): beaten and thrown into a creek in daylight while bystanders filmed instead of helping; her death went viral 5 April, prompting vigils in several cities and a presidential order to investigate; the town's LGBTQ council co-director said it was the third LGBTQ killing there that year; 13 trans people were killed nationally in Q1 2025.

sources.title: Sara Millerey’s brutal murder shocked Colombia. The killings didn’t stop there | CNN
sources.claim_summary: CNN 'As Equals' investigation (6 Aug 2025): armed groups in northern Colombia posted flyers carrying kill lists threatening 'homosexuals, lesbians, rapists, trans' (Guajira flyer, March 2024); only 3 of 155 criminal investigations into LGBTQ killings reached a verdict last year (about 2%, against a 9% overall homicide-conviction rate); nearly 50 queer and trans people killed this year to date; traces the history of 'social cleansing' campaigns and the gang alliance that enforces social order in the Medellín area, including expulsion of gay and trans residents.

sources.title: ‘We are killed for what we are’: trans women in Colombia targeted by armed groups | Global development | The Guardian
sources.claim_summary: 'We are killed for what we are' (30 Jul 2024): trans women in Caquetá threatened by armed groups after flyers announced a 'social cleansing' campaign naming 'faggots, lesbians and men and women who destroy homes' as targets; a trans woman was given a week to leave town or be killed and fled; more than 40 trans women were killed the previous year (41 in 2023, 8 between Feb-Apr 2024); activists document sexual violence by armed groups against trans women, including former combatant recruitment.
